title: Throughput commitment notification, escalation, and fallback ladder
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines a customer-facing policy and internal playbook for Dedicated throughput commitments. It combines: 1) when and how we notify customers about degradation, 2) an escalation ladder (automated alerts -> account ops -> SRE), and 3) a deterministic fallback ladder that automatically adjusts routing and model variants to preserve availability while limiting credit exposure. The goal is to provide clear contract language for revenue teams and a runnable autoscale/fallback config for runtime and console teams.

Problem and motivation:
Customers buying Dedicated capacity expect predictable throughput and clear remediation when capacity is degraded. Current SLA docs focus on credit math but lack an operational notification and fallback procedure that is both customer-visible and contract-safe. We need: measurable triggers, an ordered set of mitigations (e.g., bursting to spare pool, region failover, degrade to compatible model variant), and a credit taper schedule tied to time-in-degradation and scope.

Proposed deliverables:
- Contract language snippets (notice windows, credit tiers, customer remedies) suitable for inclusion in order forms and T&Cs.
- Error-budget measurement spec: 7-day rolling window of provisioning shortfall measured as percentage of committed qps used vs served at p50/p95, with a two-metric hybrid (throughput shortfall + sustained latency increase) to avoid rewarding silent quality regressions.
- Notification & escalation ladder: automated API/webhook notices at 5%, 10%, and 25% cumulative shortfall thresholds with human escalation rules and SLAs for engineering response (first response within 1 hour for P1).
- Fallback ladder (ordered mitigations): 1) Activate reserved burst capacity; 2) Shift traffic to pre-approved fallback region; 3) Switch to an approved lower-resource model variant with explicit quality-to-cost terms; 4) Temporary request queueing with max wait time; 5) Issue credits if duration exceeds threshold. Each action will have guardrails, TTLs, and opt-out toggles for customers who disallow policy-driven model downgrades.
- Credit computation examples and a sample playbook for support and account management.

Acceptance criteria and measurable outputs are below.

Support and SRE runbook produced and reviewed with oncall for all escalation steps

sample_contract_snippets: Operational notice: Redwood will provide electronic notice when measured dedicated throughput for the Customer falls below the committed throughput by more than 10% during a rolling 7-day window. Notices will include the scope, estimated impact, and applied mitigations.

Credits: For verified sustained degradation (>=10% shortfall for more than 2 consecutive hours), Customer will receive service credits equal to X% of the monthly committed fee per hour of degradation, subject to a cap of 30% of the monthly committed fee per billing cycle. Credits are sole remedy unless otherwise specified.

Fallbacks: During capacity degradation Redwood may automatically apply mitigations from the agreed fallback ladder (reserved burst -> region failover -> model variant -> queueing). Redwood will notify the Customer before applying mitigations that materially change model outputs. Customers may opt-out of model-variant fallbacks by specifying 'no-model-downgrade' in the account SLA settings.
